interface.evidence: Original problem lists two 2-bit inputs A[1:0], B[1:0] and one-bit output z.

semantics.function: z is 1 when A equals B, otherwise 0 for binary inputs
semantics.timing: Combinational; output follows current inputs with no added cycle latency
semantics.clock_reset: None: original interface has no clock or reset
semantics.initialization: No stored state or initialization required; original problem specifies no initial value
semantics.evidence: Original problem describes a circuit producing z based on equality of A and B without sequential ports or timing requirements.

numeric.input_domain: Two-bit unsigned binary vectors, values 0 through 3
numeric.arithmetic: No arithmetic, rounding, saturation, or overflow

verification.oracle: Independent explicit truth table from original equality requirement
verification.coverage: All 16 binary A/B combinations, repeated in reverse order to check changing inputs
verification.sampling: Sample one simulation time unit after each input change for combinational settling; no clock edges
verification.success: Print line beginning PASS only after every comparison succeeds

specification_ambiguities.evidence: Original problem does not define behavior for X or Z inputs
specification_ambiguities.resolution: Use normal logical equality in RTL; required development oracle covers all specified binary combinations without inventing X/Z requirements
